We examine the phenomenology within an extended "2N2"—or more simply "22"—model, building upon its minimal basis of two additional neutrino singlet states. This includes both the seesaw mechanism for neutrino mass generation and dark matter in the form of a weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP). Specifically, we explore the decay dynamics of extra gauge bosons and other collider signatures, as well as precision measurements involving neutral current processes, all aimed at testing the predictiveness of the minimal "2N2" framework. We further analyze the conditions for a stable Higgs vacuum and derive the parametric limits for dark matter's absolute stability. Key physical predictions from the minimal basis are highlighted, including the precise mass of neutrinos and dark matter.
